blocks.text: Condo buildings in Edmonds
Kings Crossing 2 (King Crossing Tower 2) — 7358 Edmonds Street
By Cressey; built 2020, 37 storeys (listing-aggregator source).
Kings Crossing 1 — 7388 Kingsway
By Cressey; current listings describe a modern concrete tower with air conditioning, clubhouse, sauna and steam, and outdoor theatre, walking distance to SkyTrain, shopping and the community centre.
Toscana — 7738 Edmonds Street

Built in 2012: a four-storey, 49-unit wood-frame low-rise with fibre-cement and glass siding. One listing says "No Pets or Rentals", and another says no pets. A pet ban can still be enforced, but rental bans have been void since November 24, 2022.
Azure at Southgate City — 7683 Park Crescent

Azure, by Ledingham McAllister, completed in 2024: a 30-storey tower plus a four-storey low-rise (the Teal Collection), the first phase of the 52-acre Southgate City community, two blocks from Edmonds SkyTrain Station. The developer used 7662 18th Street as the address, but listings also use 7788 18th Street, so check the strata's address for a specific unit. A presale source gives 282 units in the tower, and a project source 320 homes in the phase, including 53 in the Teal Collection; the strata plan settles it.
Azure 2 at Southgate City — 7769 Park Crescent

By Ledingham McAllister; built 2024, 28 storeys, concrete construction with freehold strata tenure (current listings). A presale record gives 320 units (presale source). Current listings describe air conditioning, concierge and fitness centre amenities, and record pets as "Cats OK" on one listing.
Cedar Creek — 7133 14th Avenue, with further buildings at 7579 / 7588 16th Street and 7599 15th Street

By Ledingham McAllister; a low-rise community built 2021 at the 14th Avenue building, with listings dating the 16th Street building to 2022 and the 15th Street building to 2023 as the community phased in — treat the year as building-specific.
Streets, schools and transit near Edmonds condos

items.t: Edmonds is in southeast Burnaby, centred on Kingsway at Edmonds Street around Edmonds Station, and is one of Burnaby's four town centres. "Edmonds" is the real estate board's name for the area (listings also show "Edmonds BE"). The City publishes no boundary for the MLS® area; the Edmonds Community Plan (adopted March 2025) divides the centre into six districts: Central Edmonds, South Edmonds, the Station District, West Edmonds, Northwest Edmonds and East Edmonds.

Main roads: Kingsway and Edmonds Street, with Griffiths Drive and 18th Avenue serving the station area and Canada Way / 10th Avenue linking east toward New Westminster. Royal Oak and Metrotown are to the west, Highgate sits within the town centre's east side, and South Slope is to the south-west.

The condos are in two areas: the Kingsway and Highgate area (Cressey's Kings Crossing towers at Kingsway and Edmonds Street, and older low-rises on Edmonds Street such as Toscana), and South Edmonds and Southgate City, Ledingham McAllister's planned community south of the station (Azure, Azure 2 and the Cedar Creek low-rises on 14th Avenue, 15th Street and 16th Street). The streets away from Kingsway are still detached houses.

Across Burnaby that month, condos and townhomes had a median sale price of $686,000, at $763 per square foot, selling for 98% of list price in 36 days on average (SnapStats GVR September 2026). These are city-wide figures; no median is published for Edmonds alone.

Transit anchor: Edmonds Station on the Expo Line, with a bus loop; TransLink route 116 also links Edmonds Station to Metrotown Station via Imperial, Sussex, Marine Drive, Marine Way, Byrne Road, Southridge Drive, Griffiths Drive and 18th Avenue, serving south Edmonds street by street.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Edmonds

items.t: Burnaby zoning and plans: the governing bylaw is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, adopted June 9, 2026 and in effect July 1, 2026 — the former Zoning Bylaw No. 4742 (1965) is not current and must not be cited as current. Burnaby's R1 SSMUH District (June 2024) allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, with multi-unit lots able to be stratified. The Edmonds Community Plan was adopted in March 2025, and the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan (adopted December 9, 2025) replaces the 1998 OCP and takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict.

blocks.text: Good to know about Edmonds condos

items.t: Azure carries three addresses. The strata address in listings is 7683 Park Crescent, the developer's presentation centre was at 7662 18th Street, and unit listings also appear at 7788 18th Street — one building, three addresses in the wild. Confirm which address the specific unit's title and strata records use before ordering documents.
Southgate City is a 15-to-20-year build-out, and Azure is only phase one.

Cedar Creek's buildings were phased a year apart. Listings date 7133 14th Avenue to 2021, 7579 16th Street to 2022 and 7599 15th Street to 2023 — same developer, same community name, three different warranty and depreciation-report positions. Compare the specific building's documents, not the community's marketing.

The town centre got a brand-new plan in 2025 — and then the citywide OCP changed over it. The Edmonds Community Plan was adopted in March 2025; the Burnaby 2050 OCP followed on December 9, 2025 and takes precedence over older community-plan maps where they conflict; the Kingsway + Edmonds master plan is expressly under review to align with the new OCP. Listing copy citing pre-2025 Edmonds planning is out of date.

Route 116 is the south Edmonds workhorse. Beyond the SkyTrain, TransLink route 116 runs Metrotown Station to Edmonds Station via Griffiths Drive, Southridge Drive and 18th Avenue — the bus the Cedar Creek and Southgate streets actually live on, and the one listing copy rarely names.

items.t: The townhouses are in three places: the Stride Avenue corridor south of the station (Riverstone, Kensington, Eden at Edmonds and Maplewood Terrace, plus Sylvan Court on Edmonds Street); around 17th Avenue and Leeside (Leeside Creek, Element 1 and Element 2); and the South Edmonds edge of Southgate City on 14th to 16th Avenues (Kingsgate Gardens and the Southgate townhomes at 7333 16th Avenue). The streets away from Kingsway are still detached houses.
At the Burnaby community level that month, Condos & Townhomes posted a median sale price of $686,000; $763/sqft; sale-to-list 98%; 36 days on market.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Edmonds

items.t: For all 11 strata complexes, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Rental and pet lines in listings aren't the bylaws. Age matters here: Kensington (1992) and Sylvan Court (1990) are well into their repair cycles, while Element 2 (2025) is still in its first years and under warranty.

blocks.text: Good to know about Edmonds townhomes

items.t: Two complexes share the street number 7128 — on different streets. Leeside Creek is at 7128 17th Avenue (2005) and Riverstone is at 7128 Stride Avenue (2003). Document orders, courier directions and even listing searches routinely cross them; confirm the street, not just the number, before ordering a Form B.

Southgate City is a 15-to-20-year build-out, and the townhouses predate the towers. The 7333 16th Avenue townhouse complex (2007) and Kingsgate Gardens (2010) were built years before Azure, Southgate City's first tower phase, completed in 2024 — a Southgate townhouse buyer owns the low-rise edge of a master plan whose later towers still require separate rezonings.

Edmonds Community Centre is the amenity the strata fees don't buy. At 7433 Edmonds Street it has a 6-lane pool, a leisure pool with waterslides and a lazy river, steam room and sauna, two gyms and the Edmonds Centre for 55+; the Tommy Douglas Library branch serves this quadrant at the Kingsway node and the Edmonds UPCC is at #201-7315 Edmonds St — the civic package beside the Stride/17th Avenue complexes.

On the south edge, check the ravine. Byrne Creek Ravine Park runs south from the town centre along Byrne Creek, and Ron McLean Park is on the south side by the ravine. For lots and complexes backing onto the ravine, check watercourse setbacks and development permit conditions early, because they tend to come up late in a deal.

Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established house lots

The only lot-size figures are the R1 zone's thresholds (280 m² and 281 m²). What matters more is location: lots near Kingsway and the station fall under the six districts of the March 2025 Edmonds Community Plan, and lots on the ravine edge have Byrne Creek setbacks to check.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.
ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Edmonds.

Market figures, September 2026 (homes, not land): in Edmonds, 9 detached homes were listed and 2 sold (22%), and 89 condos and townhomes were listed and 7 sold (8%). Burnaby's medians were $1,825,000 for detached homes and $686,000 for condos and townhomes.

items.t: Southgate City — South Edmonds (former Safeway distribution site, framed by 11th and 14th Avenues and 15th and 18th Streets; developer Ledingham McAllister): The Edmonds Community Plan names Southgate City as the master-planned community in South Edmonds, planned around the Southgate City node. Land position taken here: Southgate City is assembled, built development land — a buyer buys a strata home in it, not a lot.

Kingsway + Edmonds — southwest corner of Kingsway and Edmonds (City of Burnaby / BC Housing, publicly owned 4.5-acre site). Proposal only: Nothing on this site is for sale as land or as homes on this evidence.

items.t: Edmonds is in southeast Burnaby, centred on Kingsway at Edmonds Street around Edmonds Station, and is one of Burnaby's four town centres. It's also the real estate board's name for the area. The City doesn't publish a boundary, but the Edmonds Community Plan (adopted March 2025) splits the town centre into districts including Central Edmonds, South Edmonds, the Station District, West Edmonds, Northwest Edmonds and East Edmonds; Northwest Edmonds runs roughly from Gilley Avenue east to Walker and Griffiths Avenues, and from Imperial Street south to Beresford Street.
Nearby areas: Royal Oak and Metrotown to the west, Highgate within the town centre's east side, East Burnaby and the City of New Westminster to the east, South Slope to the south-west.

Main roads and transit: Kingsway and Edmonds Street are the main roads, with Griffiths Drive and 18th Avenue serving the station area and Canada Way / 10th Avenue linking east toward New Westminster. Edmonds Station is on the Expo Line; route 116 runs between Metrotown Station and Edmonds Station via Griffiths Drive, Southridge Drive and 18th Avenue.

Nearby: Edmonds Community Centre (7433 Edmonds Street), with pools, gyms and the Edmonds Centre for 55+; the Tommy Douglas Library on Kingsway; the Edmonds Urgent and Primary Care Centre (#201-7315 Edmonds Street); and Byrne Creek Ravine Park and Taylor Park (7599 Mission Avenue) on the east side. The city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid Street), across the city to the northwest.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Edmonds

items.t: OCP and community plan — Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, adopted December 9, 2025: replaces the 1998 OCP and takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict; the Edmonds Community Plan was adopted in March 2025 and plans the centre in six districts (Central Edmonds, South Edmonds, the Station District, West Edmonds, Northwest Edmonds, East Edmonds). A town-centre lot's value case is read off these two documents, in that order.
Creeks: Byrne Creek runs in a ravine through the south side of the area (Byrne Creek Ravine Park; Ron McLean Park, 7820 Hedley Ave).

blocks.text: Good to know about Edmonds lots

items.t: The town centre got two new governing documents in nine months: the Edmonds Community Plan in March 2025 and the Burnaby 2050 OCP on December 9, 2025 — and the Kingsway + Edmonds master plan is explicitly under review to align with the new OCP, so a land memo written off the pre-2025 plan framework is stale on its face.

Southgate's townhouses predate its towers by 17 years: the 7333 16th Avenue townhouse complex (2007) and Kingsgate Gardens (2010) were built years before Azure, Southgate City's first tower phase, completed in 2024 — a Southgate-edge lot or townhouse sits at the low-rise edge of a master plan whose later towers still require separate rezonings.

The bus the South Edmonds streets actually live on is route 116: Metrotown Station to Edmonds Station via Imperial, Sussex, Marine Drive, Marine Way, Byrne Road, Southridge Drive, Griffiths Drive and 18th Avenue — the street-by-street service behind the station-area lots, and the route listing copy rarely names.

faq.a: Age and type of building: on Kingsway, there are Cressey's Kings Crossing towers (Tower 2 built in 2020) and the 2012 wood-frame Toscana low-rise. South Edmonds has Ledingham McAllister's Southgate City (Azure and Azure 2, finished in 2024) and its Cedar Creek low-rises (2021–2023). All of them compare against the same Burnaby median for condos and townhomes ($686,000, September 2026), but warranty coverage, construction (concrete or wood frame) and depreciation reports differ building by building.
faq.q: Kingsway towers or Southgate — what's the real difference?

faq.a: Renting, yes for a long-term tenancy: rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022. The pet prohibition is different — pet bylaws remain enforceable, and a current Toscana listing records pets as "No." Treat the rental line as void and the pet line as live until the registered bylaws on the Form B say otherwise.
faq.q: Toscana says "No Pets or Rentals" — can I rent it out? Can I bring a dog?

faq.a: No. Hall Towers (7264 Kingsway) is 331 units of BC Housing non-market rental housing owned by the Provincial Rental Housing Corporation — there is nothing to buy, and it is slated for replacement under the Kingsway + Edmonds master plan without displacing tenants.
faq.q: Is Hall Towers a condo building I can buy into?

faq.a: Both: Stride Avenue has Riverstone (2003), Kensington (1992), Eden at Edmonds (2012) and Maplewood Terrace (2006), with Sylvan Court (1990) on Edmonds Street; 17th Avenue has Leeside Creek (2005), Element 1 (2020) and Element 2 (2025). The Stride complexes are older and larger; the 17th Avenue ones are newer and closer to the station.
faq.q: Stride Avenue or 17th Avenue — where is the townhouse choice?

faq.a: Long-term, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022. Kensington's listing data already records rentals allowed. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw — read the registered bylaws in the Form B package.
faq.q: Can I rent out my Edmonds townhouse?

faq.a: Element 2's marketing puts Edmonds Station 600 m away; Leeside Creek listings put the walk at 5 minutes; Kensington is described as a short stroll to Edmonds SkyTrain Station. Edmonds Station is on the Expo Line. Measure the walk for the specific complex — the Stride Avenue addresses sit farther south than the 17th Avenue ones.
faq.q: How far is the SkyTrain, honestly?

faq.a: Yes. Edmonds is one of Burnaby's four town centres, centred on Kingsway at Edmonds Street around Edmonds Station on the Expo Line, and the City adopted a new Edmonds Community Plan in March 2025.

It depends on the address. In-area SD41 schools include Edmonds Community Elementary (K–7), 7651 18th Ave, Twelfth Avenue Elementary (K–7) and Byrne Creek Community Secondary (8–12), 7777 18th St; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.
faq.q: Which schools serve an Edmonds address?

faq.a: Edmonds Station is on the Expo Line with a bus loop; route 116 also links Edmonds Station to Metrotown Station through south Burnaby via Griffiths Drive, Southridge Drive and Marine Way.
